findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

During the inspection the hand sink in the dish area is observed with containers on top of it and other containers in front of it. These block use of the only hand sink in this area. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintain all hand sinks accessible at all times in the facility in order to allow for, and promote, good hand washing practices. The items were removed during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket in the back of the facility was observed to barely produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. The kitchen manager was shown and education conducted. The bucket was remade to correct. Ensure that all in use sanitizers are maintained at effective levels in the facility at all times.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

The PIC during this inspection was unaware of any completed allergen trainings at this facility. They are instructed to have all CFPMs at the facility complete an ANSI accredited allergen training and maintain copies of the certificates at the facility moving forward.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

The PIC during this inspection was unaware of signed reporting agreements or similar paperwork available in the facility. The situation was discussed and fresh copies will be sent via email. Ensure copies are signed for each food handler prior to the scheduled follow up.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

1) On arrival the hand sink behind the register is observed with a cup in it. 2) During the inspection the hand sink in the dish area is observed with containers on top of it and other containers in front of it. These block use of the only hand sink in this area. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintained all hand sinks accessible at all times in the facility in order to allow for and promote good hand washing practices. The items were removed during this inspection to correct both situations.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The standing cooler behind the registers is observed to be holding TCS foods between 48F and 52F internal temperatures. Multiple items were checked using a probe thermometer that were representative of the coolers functionality. TCS items were then discarded and included: 1) a containers of goat cheese; 2) two containers of sour cream; 3) a container of macaroni salad; 4) three quarter pans of sliced tomatoes; 5) three containers of Greek yogurt; 6) three quarter pans of house made avocado spread and; 7) a container of potato salad. Cooked eggs and bacon were recently placed into this cooler after preparation this morning and were allowed to be moved to other coolers in the facility. Many other items such as pre-packaged salad dressings and alcohol are not considered TCS foods and were allowed to remain in this cooler. As the TCS foods were discarded the violation is being considered CORRECTED at this time. The cooler functionality is being managed under line item #33 of this report.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The standing cooler behind the registers is observed to not be functioning correctly (refer to line item #22 for write up). The foods were taken care of on line item #22, but the cooler repair is being managed on this line item. Ensure that a refrigerator tech conducts maintenance on this equipment prior to the follow-up. 10 days would land on a Sunday and the following Monday is a holiday. The follow up is scheduled for the Tuesday as it is the next available day.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.citation_text:
4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. 

The probe thermometer in the facility is observed approximately 6F - 10F off of accurate during this inspection. The thermometer was checked using ice water and registered in the mid 20s Fahrenheit. Education was conducted for calibrating this type thermometer and the PIC is instructed to ensure that all thermometers are correctly calibrated at all times.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.citation_text:
3-602.11(A) Food Labels. (A) FOOD PACKAGED in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, shall be labeled as specified in LAW, including 21 CFR 101 - Food labeling, and 9 CFR 317 Labeling, marking devices, and containers. 

The packages used for Fed Kitchen do not have cooking temperature requirements as per the HACCP plan and previous conversations with the PIC. The situation was discussed with multiple PICs and new labels are in the works for the next batch to be prepared. Ensure that all labeling requirements are met on the food packaging and per the HACCP plan at al times.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

The PIC during this inspection is unaware of any completed allergen trainings at this facility. They recalled a previous conversation. They are instructed to have all CFPMs at the facility complete an ANSI accredited allergen training and maintain copies of the certificates at the facility moving forward.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink in the kitchen area of the facility is without paper towels during this inspection. The PIC was shown and replaced the empty dispenser during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

1) Raw chicken is observed over Ready-To-Eat (RTE) turkey and cooked beef in the walk in cooler. 2) Raw ground turkey is observed over RTE ground beef in the walk in cooler. Both items were shown to the PIC and they adjusted the storage locations to correct. Education should be regular and consistent in relation to storage orders in the coolers moving forward. Ensure foods are stored correctly in relation to their cooking temperatures in the coolers.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

An open can of mountain dew was observed on the wire shelf in the dry storage room intermixed with foods intended for consumers. Before the PIC could be shown the can was removed by staff. The situation was discussed with the PIC. They asked for suggestions and the inspector stated that personal drinks should be stored “low and/or away” from items intended for consumers.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The ice scoop at the drive thru window is observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This allows for bare hand contact with the ice when the scoop is picked up. The issue was discussed with the PIC and the scoop moved to correct. Ensure that the utensils are handled in ways where there is not a concern of contaminating the foods they are intended to handle.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

White mold is observed on diced tomatoes in a container in the bottom of one of the prep coolers. The PIC was shown and discarded the food to correct the violation. Ensure that all foods are maintained in a safe stated through service.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The deflector shield of the ice machine was observed with pink, green and black mold growth along the bottom edge. The location was discussed with the PIC and cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine in the facility would not register a sanitizer concentration on the inspector’s test strips over multiple attempts. While investigating it appears that the container of concentrate has off gassed and diluted itself naturally. This was discussed with the PIC and a new jug attached to the machine in an attempt to resolve the situation. Once primed the machine began dispensing chemical at acceptable levels. Ensure that the sanitizers used in the facility are maintained at effective levels at all times.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

1) A squeeze bottle in one of the prep coolers has a marked date of 5/11-5/18. The PIC indicated that it should be 6/11-6/18 and replaced the label to correct. 2) Sliced tomatoes in the bottom section of another prep coolers have a marked date of 6/-6/12. This container was discarded during this inspection to correct. 3) A different container of diced tomatoes is without any date marking. This container was discarded due to observed mold growth (refer to line item # 13 for write up). Ensure that all Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are correctly marked for seven day date marking at all times.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

There is a gap that runs along the entire bottom of the walk in cooler door. The PIC was shown and discussed the situation. The owner latter asked for suggestions as this has been an ongoing issue with the delivery drivers. The walk in cooler is located outside of the back door at this facility and several issues could develop due to this in the future, but have not appeared yet. The current concern is that pests have easy entrance into the walk in cooler from outside. There are not pests currently observed at this time. Ensure that the door is repaired prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all outer openings to the facility are sealed to protect against pest entry.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival and throughout the walk through sani buckets or other sanitizing methods were not available for use in the food preparation and handling areas. The PIC was notified and  sani buckets were prepared for both the front and back preparation areas to correct. Ensure that sanitizers are available for use at all times in the facility that foods are being handled/prepared.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). 

Under the hand sink in the dish area the coving has come undone from the wall exposing a gap between the wall and floor. The PIC was shown and instructed to re-cove the location to prevent moisture or detritus accumulation. Ensure that all wall/floor junctions are closed to allow for effective cleaning.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

The caulking between the three part sink and the wall is observed completely black along most of the strip. The PIC was shown and instructed to replace the caulking with new prior to the next routine inspection and to maintain it clean moving forward.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x3) 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

A Certified Food Protection Manager is not available at this facility during this inspection This is the fourth inspection in a row where this violation has been noted. Ensure that there are sufficient CFPM’s so that there is one at the facility at all times that food handling and handling of food contact surfaces is taking place.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the proper cleaning procedure in order to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms.

Multiple hand washing procedures are observed throughout the inspection where the employee used their bare hands to turn off the faucet at the end of hand washing. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to review hand washing with all employees and ensure that proper hand washing is taking place at all times moving forward.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) Multiple tea jugs in the standing coolers next to the drive thru window are observed with sticker residue and other debris still remaining on the containers. 2) The blender jugs next to the drive thru window are observed soiled after cleaning. Two of the containers had debris floating in the water at the bottom of the container and the third had what appears to be berry juice on it. The PIC was shown and the items moved to dish for re-cleaning. More thorough cleaning of these items should be taking place between uses.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Multiple moist rags are observed on counters in the facility. Education was conducted and the rags moved back to sani buckets to correct. Ensure that all wiping cloths are stored between uses in solution of sufficient concentration.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

1) The container used for coffee cup lid plugs is observed soiled and in need of cleaning. The plugs are dumped into this container and come into direct contact with it. Education was conducted and the PIC moved the container to dish for cleaning. The current batch of plugs were discarded. 2) Stacks of to-go containers are on a shelf above the steam table with the food contact surfaces facing up/exposed. This was discussed with he PIC and the items flipped over to correct. Ensure that all single service food contact surfaces are protected from contamination at all times.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

A pair of shoes (flops) are observed stored on top of cases of water bottles in the dry storage area. The PIC was shown and removed the items during this inspection to correct. Ensure employee clothing is stored separately from items intended for consumers moving forward.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

Multiple partially consumed water bottles are observed intermixed with consumer foods in standing coolers in the facility. The PIC was shown and removed the items to correct the immediate violation. Ensure employee foods/drinks are stored separately from foods intended for consumers so as to prevent possible contamination concerns.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

On arrival there was not a CFPM at the facility overseeing operations. Ensure that a CFPM is available at the facility at all times that food handling operations are taking place.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles.

An employee was observed not using a clean barrier to turn off faucet. Education was conducted to correct.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-301.11: (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P).

Ice scoop was stored handle down in the ice holding machine at the drive thru. Education was provided and scoop moved to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Deflector shield in the ice machine was observed to be moldy. Education was provided and violation was corrected on site by cleaning and sanitizing the shield.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Two knives were observed to be soiled with food debris on the magnetic storage rack. Education was provided, and knives were cleaned to correct.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

Towel was left on tabletop in the drive thru service area. Education was provided and the towel was returned to the sani-bucket to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Triple sink observed to have mold on the caulk connecting it to the dish room wall. PIC was notified of the issue and instructed to remove and replace damaged caulk prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (K) proper sanitizing.

The  sanitizer dispenser is not producing effective concentrations in the sani buckets used in the facility. Buckets were made manually as a temporary measure (refer to line item #16) and a follow up is being set for 10 days to ensure that the equipment is working effectively.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

On arrival there was not a CFPM at the facility overseeing operations. A CFPM arrived during the inspection to correct the violation. The PIC asked for and was given a copy of the known course locations for our area. Ensure that a CFPM is available at the facility at all times that food handling operations are taking place.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observed to change from non-food handling practices to food handling practices without washing their hands. Education was conducted to correct. The PIC is instructed to review with all staff and ensure that proper hand washing is taking place at al times that it is required.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink in the dish area is without paper towels at the beginning of this inspection. The PIC was notified and paper towels supplied to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times to promote effective hand washing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

The hand sink in the dish area is not dispensing soap at the beginning of this inspection. The PIC was notified and found that the dispenser was full, but still not dispensing. It appears that the batteries had failed and needed replacing. This tok place and the equipment is functioning correctly at the end of the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

Multiple ladles are observed stored in the dish area as clean, with food debris remaining on them. The PIC was shown and the items moved back to dish for cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani buckets at the beginning of the inspection are observed to either not register on inspector’s test strips or register low on inspector test strips. Investigation showed that the solution coming out of the dispenser is registering low or barely effective. The buckets were remade manually with both the sanitizer concentrate and tablets to allow for continued service. Refer to line item #1 for a follow up to ensure that machine is functioning correctly.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred.

The deflector shield of the ice machine is observed with several black spots, believed to be mold, observable during this inspection. The PIC was shown and cleaned the item during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that the equipment is cleaned often enough to remain clean.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

Two sets of to-go containers are on a prep counter with the food contact surfaces facing up/ exposed. Employee was consulted and instructed to store these items with the food contact surfaces protected/ down. Employee flipped the containers over (food contact surface down) to correct.
